sections.h2: How a deed is recorded in Geauga County
sections.html:
A Geauga County deed passes through three offices in Chardon, and the county publishes a one-page reference sheet, effective June 30, 2026, that lays out the order. First the Engineer approves the legal description. Next the Auditor transfers the parcel and takes the conveyance fee. Last, the Recorder files the deed and sends it back.

Geauga sits in Ohio's northeast corner inside the Cleveland metropolitan area, with Chardon as its seat.

The reference sheet lists three stops, their addresses and what each one needs from you.

  • County Engineer, 12665 Merritt Rd, Chardon, phone (440) 279-1800: reviews the legal description and stamps it with an original (wet) stamp. No fee. Allow 2 to 3 business days. Bring a legible copy of the prior deed with its volume and page reference.
  • County Auditor, 231 Main St, Suite 1-A, phone (440) 279-1600: transfers the property and updates the tax records. Needs the original signed and notarized deed.
  • County Recorder, 231 Main St, Suite 1-C, phone (440) 279-2020: records the deed and mails the original back.

The Auditor is two doors down the hall from the Recorder. To send a deed by mail, enclose a brief letter saying what you want done, your phone number, a stamped return envelope and two separate checks, payable to the Recorder and to the Auditor.

The Auditor charges $4.00 per $1,000 of transfer value and $0.50 per parcel, and checks for both are made payable to the Geauga County Auditor. Fee questions go to the Auditor.

Ohio law explains the split. The first layer is the statement-of-value fee in R.C. 319.54(G)(3), ten cents on each hundred dollars. The second is a county tax capped at thirty cents per hundred under R.C. 322.02, which the grantor pays to the Auditor ahead of recording. Some transfers are exempt, among them spousal and parent-to-child gifts, deals with no consideration and certain trust moves.

Send a completed DTE 100 or DTE 100EX conveyance form with the deed. A Transfer on Death Affidavit is the exception: it has no Auditor fee.

State law fixes the Recorder's charge at $34.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 for each page that follows. A check that is short or too large gets the document returned unrecorded, so count pages before writing it.

Electronic recording of conveyances is available and lets you skip the paper steps. Legal descriptions presented that way do not need the wet Engineer stamp. Call (440) 279-2020 to confirm what the office will take before you rely on it.

Paper filings move fast. The Recorder turns documents around the same day, and an electronic recording is returned when it is recorded. Leave a self-addressed stamped envelope with an in-person deed, or come back the next day to pick it up.

Each deed needs the following before it reaches the counter.

  • Legible signatures, and printed names under any that are hard to read.
  • A line naming whoever prepared the deed.
  • Notary acknowledgments for each grantor.
  • Original wet stamps from the Engineer and the Auditor.
  • The 8-digit permanent parcel numbers.
  • A completed conveyance form.

The extra $20 for a non-standard document comes from R.C. 317.114, which wants at least ten point type, black or blue ink and three blank inches above the text on page one. Staff cannot notarize or give legal advice, and state law keeps them from running title searches. The Recorder no longer accepts Torrens registered land filings, and it does not sell blank forms.

Geauga County has no tract (geographical) indexing, and only the indexes of recorded documents are online, so a full copy of an old deed means a copy request. Copies made by the public cost ten cents a page, while a copy made with staff help is two dollars a page.

  • Releases and assignments do not need a legal description, but they do carry the $4.00 marginal notation fee.
  • Soldier discharge records (DD214) are recorded, and a recorded discharge is what the office uses to issue a military ID card.
  • For a blank form, try a title company, an attorney or an office supply store.
  • The office will not search the title for you, and it will not notarize or give legal advice.

A shortage or overage on the check sends the document back unrecorded, so call (440) 279-2020 with the page count if you are unsure. The mailing address and the delivery address are the same, 231 Main Street, Suite 1-C, so a courier and the postal service reach one door.

The 2020 population was 95,397, and the July 2025 estimate is 95,676. Owner-occupancy is 87.2 percent, the median owned home is valued at $331,100, and median household income is $107,860. Builders pulled 180 permits in 2025.

Chardon, Burton, Middlefield, South Russell and Hunting Valley are the municipalities. In November 2024 voters dissolved the Village of Aquilla, and a transition board oversees the change.

Because three offices touch every deed, a cash sale still takes a few days of stops. Start with the Engineer's stamp, since it can take 2 to 3 business days, and line up the notary, your photo ID and both checks in the meantime.

Before you leave home, check the deed against the list above: signatures legible, preparer named, notary block complete, parcel numbers present and the conveyance form attached. A deed that comes back for a missing item costs you another trip through all three offices. If you are mailing it, count the pages first so the Recorder's check is exact, and keep copies of everything you send. Ask your title company whether it prefers to handle the filings for you, since many do it as part of closing. Either way, you sign the deed in front of a notary, so bring a photo ID.

faqs.q: What are the total charges to record a deed in Geauga County?
faqs.a: At the Recorder, plan on $34.00 for two pages, $8.00 for each extra one and $20.00 more for a non-standard deed. The Auditor bills $4.00 per $1,000 of value and $0.50 per parcel on its own.

faqs.q: Do I need the County Engineer for a Geauga County deed?
faqs.a: Yes, for paper filings. The Engineer reviews and approves the legal description with an original stamp at no fee, usually within 2 to 3 business days. Legal descriptions sent through electronic recording are the exception.

faqs.q: Where is the Geauga County Recorder located?
faqs.a: At 231 Main Street, Suite 1-C, Chardon, Ohio 44024. Call (440) 279-2020. The County Auditor is in Suite 1-A of the same building.

faqs.q: Will the Recorder search the title to my house?
faqs.a: No. State law prohibits the office from doing title searches. Try the online index of recorded documents, or hire a title company or an attorney.

faqs.q: How long does recording take in Chardon?
faqs.a: The Recorder turns documents around the same day. Mailed deeds come back to you after recording in the self-addressed stamped envelope you include, and an electronic recording is returned when it is recorded.
